## Part I: Integration by Parts

**1.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$I = \int x^3 \ln x \, dx$$

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 1
$u = \ln x,\ dv = x^3\,dx \Rightarrow du = \frac{1}{x}dx,\ v = \frac{x^4}{4}$
$$= \frac{x^4}{4}\ln x - \int \frac{x^3}{4}\,dx = \frac{x^4}{4}\ln x - \frac{x^4}{16} + C$$
:::

**2.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$I = \int x^4 e^x \, dx$$

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 2
Tabular method (differentiate $x^4$, integrate $e^x$, alternate signs):
$$= e^x\left(x^4 - 4x^3 + 12x^2 - 24x + 24\right) + C$$
:::

**3.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$I = \int \tan^{-1} x \, dx$$

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 3
$u = \tan^{-1}x,\ dv = dx \Rightarrow du = \frac{1}{1+x^2}dx,\ v = x$
$$= x\tan^{-1}x - \int \frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx = x\tan^{-1}x - \frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2) + C$$
:::

**4.** (10 points) Evaluate the definite integral
$$\int_1^e x \ln x \, dx$$

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 4
$u = \ln x,\ dv = x\,dx \Rightarrow v = \frac{x^2}{2}$
$$= \left[\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x - \frac{x^2}{4}\right]_1^e = \left(\frac{e^2}{2} - \frac{e^2}{4}\right) - \left(0 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{e^2 + 1}{4}$$
:::

## Part II: Trigonometric Integrals

**5.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$\int \cos^4 x \, dx$$

*Hint:* $\sin^2 x = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}$ and $\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}$.

<div class="work-lg"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 5
$$\cos^4 x = \left(\frac{1+\cos 2x}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{8} + \frac{1}{2}\cos 2x + \frac{1}{8}\cos 4x$$
$$\int \cos^4 x\,dx = \frac{3x}{8} + \frac{\sin 2x}{4} + \frac{\sin 4x}{32} + C$$
:::

**6.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$I = \int \sin^5 x \cos^2 x \, dx$$

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 6
Odd power of sine: save one $\sin x$, let $u = \cos x$, $du = -\sin x\,dx$.
$$= \int (1-\cos^2 x)^2\cos^2 x\,\sin x\,dx = -\int (u^2 - 2u^4 + u^6)\,du$$
$$= -\frac{\cos^3 x}{3} + \frac{2\cos^5 x}{5} - \frac{\cos^7 x}{7} + C$$
:::

**7.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$I = \int \cos x \sin 2x \, dx$$

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 7
Using $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$ and $u = \cos x$:
$$= \int 2\cos^2 x\sin x\,dx = -\frac{2}{3}\cos^3 x + C$$
(Equivalent via product-to-sum: $-\tfrac{1}{2}\cos x - \tfrac{1}{6}\cos 3x + C$.)
:::

**8.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$\int 4 \cos x \sin 2x \cos 3x \, dx$$

*Hint:* Use product-to-sum identities, e.g. $2\sin A\cos B = \sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)$.

<div class="work"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 8
$2\sin 2x\cos x = \sin 3x + \sin x$, so the integrand is
$$2(\sin 3x + \sin x)\cos 3x = 2\sin 3x\cos 3x + 2\sin x\cos 3x = \sin 6x + \sin 4x - \sin 2x$$
$$\int 4\cos x\sin 2x\cos 3x\,dx = -\frac{\cos 6x}{6} - \frac{\cos 4x}{4} + \frac{\cos 2x}{2} + C$$
:::

## Part III: Partial Fractions

**9.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$\int \frac{1}{(3x-1)(6x+2)} \, dx$$

<div class="work-lg"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 9
Factor: $6x+2 = 2(3x+1)$, and $\dfrac{1}{(3x-1)(3x+1)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{3x-1} - \dfrac{1}{3x+1}\right)$, so
$$\frac{1}{(3x-1)(6x+2)} = \frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{1}{3x-1} - \frac{1}{3x+1}\right)$$
$$\int \frac{1}{(3x-1)(6x+2)}\,dx = \frac{1}{12}\ln\left|\frac{3x-1}{3x+1}\right| + C$$
:::

**10.** (10 points) Evaluate
$$\int \frac{1}{(x+2)^2(x-1)} \, dx$$

<div class="work-lg"></div>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 10
$\dfrac{A}{x+2} + \dfrac{B}{(x+2)^2} + \dfrac{C}{x-1}$ with $A = -\tfrac{1}{9},\ B = -\tfrac{1}{3},\ C = \tfrac{1}{9}$
$$\int \frac{1}{(x+2)^2(x-1)}\,dx = -\frac{1}{9}\ln|x+2| + \frac{1}{3(x+2)} + \frac{1}{9}\ln|x-1| + C$$
:::
